original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For the shortest five-label equation R+S+T+U+V=4I, prove by an exhaustive support census that no nonzero symmetric rational rank-one solution has all four targets as subset sums, and exhibit one five-direction solution whose parity image is all of F2^2.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the five-frame question left open by the four-call support census, for the single shortest once-each equation.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. The five-call equation admits no word, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the five-call support census and one explicit parity-image witness. Do not census six frames, and do not add an old call.
evidence: Exhaustive finite census: every target has trace 2 and determinant 1/2, so only subset sizes 2 and 3 can match, and all 116280 ordered 4-tuples fail. 71040 are invertible and off the cone, 44520 are inconsistent, and 720 freeze one frame at ±2I, ±(A-B), or ±(P-Q). Parity witness, not a census: directions (-1,1),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1),(1,3) at scales 1,-1,3,-1/2,1/2 have full parity image and are still excluded by a two-call character count. The inherited determinant and subset-sum necessity are not reproved.

open_questions.question: Can six added signed rank-one frames, each used once and with no old call, meet target support for F1+...+F6=4I?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A six-call word would still lower the eight-call minimum. The five-column census does not apply, and the complement of a four-element subset is now a pair.
open_questions.first_step: Rewrite the size lemma for six frames, keeping subset sizes 2, 3, and 4, then test one six-direction rational solution.
open_questions.blocked_by: Lemma 1 uses five frames. Size 4 is no longer the complement of a single frame, so the 116280-tuple domain does not carry over.

open_questions.question: Can five added signed rank-one frames plus one old call meet support at length 6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A length-6 word would lower the eight-call minimum. Theorem-level support failure in this package uses the residual 4I.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one old projector E and the equation R+S+T+U+V=4I-E, then repeat the subset-size test on that residual.
open_questions.blocked_by: Every identity here uses the residual 4I. One old call changes the allowed subset sizes.
